scoring._README: score = sum of the components below. Higher = more brief-worthy. Candidates are pre-sorted by score desc; each item's `score_breakdown` shows its parts.
scoring.recency: 0–1h = 2.3 (breaking) · 1–3h = 2.0 (fresh) · then linear decay to 0 by 24h · unknown = 0.5
scoring.signal: AI/tech (or watchlist) keyword hits — match_count capped at 5 × 0.6
scoring.source: outlet authority from trusted-sources.md: primary (company/lab) 2.0 · citation 1.2 · screening 0.5 · other 1.0
scoring.corrob: cross-outlet corroboration — how many outlets ran the same headline (cluster_size − 1, capped 3) × 0.8
scoring.watchlist: watchlist stream only: matched company tier — Tier-1 +1.5 · Tier-2 +0.8

candidates.body_text: Tech Industry Artificial Intelligence Z.ai powers up a 1-gigawatt AI data center built entirely on Chinese chips, report claims — GLM developer now runs multiple 10,000-chip clusters with zero Nvidia silicon News By Luke James Published 11 hours ago The blacklisted Chinese AI lab's gigawatt-class site is among the largest built by any Chinese model developer. (Image credit: UCG) Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Chinese AI developer Z.ai (formerly Zhipu) has finished building a 1GW data center stocked exclusively with domestically made chips and has switched part of it on, Bloomberg reported Monday, citing a person familiar with the matter. The facility will train the company's GLM model family, and the source told Bloomberg that Z.ai has now built or operates several computing clusters holding more than 10,000 chips apiece. A gigawatt is enough electricity to run roughly 750,000 homes, which puts the site among the largest ever stood up by a Chinese AI lab. candidates.description: Google DeepMind  today released three new proprietary AI models  it says are among its most token-efficient yet: Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, and Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber.   The models aim to make AI agents faster, smarter, and cheaper at scale. Google is pricing Gemini 3.6 Flash at $1.50
candidates.body_text: Credit: VentureBeat made with Google Gemini Google DeepMind today released three new proprietary AI models it says are among its most token-efficient yet: Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, and Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber. The models aim to make AI agents faster, smarter, and cheaper at scale. Google is pricing Gemini 3.6 Flash at $1.50 per one million input tokens and $7.50 per one million output tokens through its application programming interface (API), while Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite costs a staggeringly cheap $0.30/$2.50 per million tokens in/out. Compare that to the $1.50/$9.00 per 1M tokens for Gemini 3.5 Flash, and the $2/$12 for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, and the savings are considerable. However, Google's prior generation Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite still remains the search giant's "most cost-efficient" model at $0.25/$1.50 per 1M tokens. Yet, it remains 2X slower than the new, more expensive Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, giving those enterprises who value speed more "bang" for their buck.
